verses.1: And all the people of Judah took Uziah as their king. He was twelve years old when they made him their king, after his father Amaziah’s death.
verses.2: He built the cities and restored them to Judah, after the king’s father died.
verses.3: He reigned for thirteen years. Then he ruled for fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Kehilya, who came from Jerusalem.
verses.4: And he did what was right in the eyes of Jehovah, just as his father Amasya had done.
verses.5: And it became a place of prayer for God during the days of Zerachiah, who understood God’s will through his visions. And during the time when he prayed to Jehovah, God was successful in his efforts.
verses.6: And he went out and fought against the Philistines. He destroyed their cities, along with the cities of Jabesh Gilead and Jabesh Ashdod. He built cities in Ashdod and among the Philistines.
verses.7: And God helped him against the Philistines and against those who lived in Gurg Ba’al and those who were rebellious.
verses.8: And the Ammonites gave gifts to Ozziah. Then he went away until he arrived in Egypt, as he had promised.
verses.9: And Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem, at the gates of the Philistines and at the gates of Gaza. He also strengthened those towers.
verses.10: And he built forts on the coast, and he dug many tunnels. For he had a great deal of land to cultivate. In the valleys and plains, there were crops and vineyards in the mountains and in the vineyards. He truly loved the land.
verses.11: And Uzziah had a army of soldiers who were trained for war. They were led by Yehiya the scribe. Their actions were overseen by Hananiyah, one of the king’s officials.
verses.12: All of the heads of the fathers are counted as rulers over hundreds and six thousand men.
verses.13: And by their side was an army of three thousand, seven hundred and fifty men who were skilled in warfare. They were there to assist the king against his enemies.
verses.14: And he provided them with various kinds of animals: shepherds, drivers, and other livestock.
verses.15: And in Jerusalem, he made plans for structures that would be built on the heights and at the edges of the walls. His name became known far and wide, as he was a man who was truly capable of helping others until he became strong enough to do more.
verses.16: And in his strength, his heart rose high, until it became despicable. But he remained faithful to his God. He went into the Temple of Jehovah to offer sacrifices on the altar of that idolater.
verses.17: And after him came Azariah, the priest, along with other priests. They were all called “priests of Jehovah.”
verses.18: And they stood before Ezekiel, the king. They said to him, “Do not you, Ezekiel, offer sacrifices to Jehovah? For the priests, the sons of Aaron, who are holy, are those who can offer sacrifices. You should not go out from the holy place; it is forbidden for you to perform any rituals in the presence of Jehovah, the God.”
verses.19: And Uzziah was angry. In his hand, he held a torch for burning incense. With his anger, he acted together with the priests. The fire blazed up in his nostrils before the priests in the Temple of Jehovah, above the altar of incense.
verses.20: And Azariah, the chief priest, along with all the priests, went to him. But he was covered in blood. They rushed away from him. He also was forced to leave, because Jehovah had struck him.
verses.21: And Ezrah, the king of Medes, ruled until his death. He lived in the palace of the judge Medes, since he was appointed from the house of God. And he judged the people of that land.
verses.22: And all the words of Uziah, both the earlier and later ones, were written down by Yeshua son of Amos, the prophet.
verses.23: And Euziah lay with his fathers. They buried him along with his fathers in the field of burial, which belongs to the kings. For they said, “He is a traitor.” And Yotham became king over him.
